text:
Theo: quick thread — ran a short smoke profile against the kernel selector with KV cache turned on; saw a ~4% p99 regression on long sequences (2k tokens). sharing notes and traces.

Maya: do you have the nsys command and whether this was sampling or full capture? :eyes:

Theo: short capture, sampling mode first (to avoid killing the box). command used: 
```
nsys profile --output=smoke220333 -t cuda,cudnn --sample=periodic --sample-interval-us=50000 --duration=30s 
  --trace-fork-before-exec=true --sample-cpu -w false -- my_inference_runner --model some-model --seq-len 2048
```
ran one full nsys (60s) afterwards for comparison but it added noticeable noise.

Grace: // quick guardrail comment // we shouldn't let any profiling run on hot prod nodes without rate limiting. what's the host selection?

Theo: ran on canary hosts in the dedicated pool (2 GPUs). sampling capture estimated overhead ~3.8% GPU time; full capture ~18% (matches what we saw). perf-bot posted the run summary: 
perf-bot: Perf summary (smoke220333): sampling overhead ≈ 3.8% GPU, 2.1% CPU; full capture overhead ≈ 17.6% GPU, 9.2% CPU.

Maya: can you paste the short kernel timeline snippet? especially curious about switchbacks between attention kernels and kv-copy.

Theo: timeline snippet (condensed):
```
[0.0ms] kernel: attention_fwd (cuda)  -> 0.90ms
[0.9ms] kernel: kv_copy (cuda memcpy) -> 0.12ms
[1.02ms] kernel: softmax (cuda) -> 0.40ms
[1.42ms] kernel: attention_bwd (cuda) -> 1.8ms
[3.22ms] kernel: attention_fwd (cuda) -> 1.05ms  <-- kernel switchback observed (different kernel variant)
[4.27ms] kernel: kv_copy -> 0.14ms (cache miss path)
```
small batches produce a lot of short kernels; we see repeated launch overhead and occasional longer kernel variants.

Grace: hypothesis: small effective batch packing + sequence padding causes frequent kernel variant selection and extra KV misses. that increases latency variability. try these quick experiments: 1) force kernel variant pin for long sequences, 2) increase batch packing threshold to prefer packing 8 small seqs before dispatch, 3) enable KV prefetch for long seqs.

Maya: agree. also propose prod-safe profiling guardrails we should adopt:
- sampling window <= 20s for regular probes
- only run on canary hosts or dedicated profiling pool
- probe rate cap 0.5% of requests per minute (circuit-breaker)
- auto-disable profiling if p99 increases >5% during probe window
- do not run full captures automatically; require opt-in with manual approval

Grace: +1 to all. add fallback routing: if kernel selector jitter observed during probe, route new long-seq requests to pinned kernel variant until probe completes.

Theo: added a tiny script to rotate profiling on/off and to collect traces to /tmp/traces/smoke220333/ (will push to GCS after sanity pass). i'll try packing threshold tweak next and run a 30s sampling vs 60s full compare.

Maya: when you run the pack experiment, include a reproducible CLI and the packed batch size, so we can correlate with the trace artifacts.

Theo: will do. initial checklist for safe rollout:
1) implement probe rate limiter (0.5%)
2) restrict to canaries
3) sampling-only by default
4) automatic rollback if p99 bump >5%
5) capture metadata: model, seq-len, batch-size, kernel-variant

Grace: sounds good. thanks — please tag us when traces uploaded. :thumbsup:

Theo: tagged @Maya @Grace when I push. ending thread for now.
